For example, one of the Bell states,

|Φ⁺⟩ = (1/√2) (|0⟩_A ⊗ |0⟩_B + |1⟩_A ⊗ |1⟩_B),

has a reduced density matrix ρ_A = Tr_B(|Φ⁺⟩⟨Φ⁺|) that is maximally mixed, ρ_A = I/2, indicating that local measurements on A alone are described by a classical probability distribution, yet joint correlations violate any local hidden-variable model, as captured by Bell inequalities.

The key point is that the global state is pure and non-factorizable, giving rise to non-classical correlations in measurement statistics. These correlations are captured by expectation values ⟨σ⃗_A · a⃗ ⊗ σ⃗_B · b⃗⟩, which can exceed bounds derived under locality and realism assumptions (e.g., CHSH ≤ 2), reaching up to 2√2.
